clue.text: What skiers introduced, good on yaws both sides of slalom's end

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing written on another simply follows it
a thing on both sides of something else flanks it, so it wraps around it

parts.note: buba is an old name for yaws, a tropical skin disease

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of slalom
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A ski instructor teaching good technique, keeping the skis yawing either side at the end of a slalom run.
explanation.walkthrough: Yaws looks like a skiing or sailing motion, but it is the tropical skin disease, recorded under an old name in Chambers; 'good on' puts its letter last.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers says the waist pouch was first worn by skiers before becoming general fashion, so this describes the item through its origin.

clue.text: Living germ one found in key region of Russia

indicators.note: what is found in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: B is a musical key
an oblast is an administrative region in Russia
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scientist discovers a living microbe in a key region of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is the musical note B, and the one sits between it and OBLAST, giving B(I)OBLAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bioblast is an old biology term for a minute unit of protoplasm, thought to be the basic living particle of a cell.

clue.text: It's working with new sound card — not sounding bad?

indicators.note: letters being worked are kneaded and reshaped like dough, ending in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A computer user is pleased that the new sound card is working and the audio no longer sounds bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a real sound card and 'working' reads as 'functioning'; in fact it signals rearranging the letters of IT, N, SOUND and CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Discordant means harsh or jarring in tone, so the negated form describes music free of jarring, clashing notes.

clue.text: A rule introduced by Michigan state

indicators.note: 'introduced by' means the pieces are put inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A new regulation is brought in by the state of Michigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is an independent country in southeast Africa, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Form of greeting regularly used by Balliol head

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one, at even intervals

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The Master of Balliol College, Oxford, has a favourite way of greeting people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across both words, so the selection does not stop at the end of Balliol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word is said both when meeting and when parting, so it is a salutation in its own right.

clue.text: Glen chap reported Sheila's depression

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: a ghyll is a ravine or glen in northern England; a guy is a chap

explanation.surface: A man from a glen reports that an Australian woman is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: GHYLL sounds like 'gill' and GUY like 'guy'. 'Sheila' is Australian slang for a woman, which signals an Australian word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilgai is a natural hollow in the ground in Australia, so it is a dip or depression in the land.

clue.text: Game not continuing after an end?

parts.note: RU is rugby union
non is the Latin and French word for not, used as a prefix

explanation.surface: A match that stops once it reaches its final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe one game, but 'not continuing' splits: 'not' is wordplay and 'continuing after an end' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-on line of verse carries its sense past the line's end without a pause, and a run-on sentence keeps going too.

clue.text: Fragment, for instance small — evidence of woodworm?

parts.note: fr. is the dictionary abbreviation for fragment
as in 'as, for example'
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A small splinter of wood, offered as a sign that woodworm is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Fragment looks like part of the woodworm picture, but it is only its abbreviation FR.
explanation.definitionFit: Frass is the powdery refuse or droppings left by wood-boring insect larvae, the telltale dust beneath beetle holes in furniture.

clue.text: Scoff not quite whole plate? This reduces available fare

parts.note: to rail at someone is to scoff at them
a punched card guiding a Jacquard loom is a perforated plate, so full of holes

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down nearly a whole plateful and wonders how to cut the cost of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff reads as eating greedily and fare as food; scoff is to jeer, and fare is the price of a journey. 'Not quite whole plate' cryptically describes a holed card.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a railcard is a pass bought once that gives discounted train tickets, cutting the price of each journey for the holder.

clue.text: I don't understand idiot turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upward means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a nana is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Someone baffled because a fool has just appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Nana is British slang for a silly person, not only a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Anan is an old Shakespearean interjection asking someone to repeat what they said, much like 'eh?' or 'pardon?'

clue.text: Pay mentioned for climbing sweep — picture's brighter with this?

indicators.note: a word that is mentioned is spoken, so its sound rather than its spelling is used

parts.note: to sink money into something is to pay it out

indicators.note: in a down entry, something climbing goes upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to lash is to sweep, as a tail does

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep is paid to climb up, and a photograph of him would come out brighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweep looks like the chimney sweep but is the verb, and pay is heard rather than written.
explanation.definitionFit: A synchroflash fires a camera's flash at exactly the moment the shutter opens, giving extra light to the photograph.

clue.text: Considered putting head of lettuce in salad

indicators.note: putting something in a word places it inside

parts.note: to see a matter is to consider it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of lettuce

explanation.surface: A cook deliberates over adding some lettuce to a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Lettuce looks like part of the salad, but only its first letter is used, slipped into SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaw, short for coleslaw, is a cold dish of shredded raw cabbage and dressing served as a side, which is a type of salad.

clue.text: Altogether naked at last

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: Sounds like a coy remark about someone finally stripping off completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altogether' tempts you towards 'in the altogether' for naked, but it is the definition; 'naked' strips the first and last letters off FINALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: In all and altogether are both used to give a total, as in 'there were ten in all'.

clue.text: Group of chemists managed in university centre in Maryland

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of this eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A team of chemists ran things at a university in Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of chemists' reads as a team of scientists; it is a chemical group, the kind chemists talk about.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranyl is the radical UO2 that behaves as a unit in compounds, and such a unit of atoms is called a group in chemistry.

clue.text: Tree in Ivory Coast, one amid meadow-grass

indicators.note: 'amid' means the pieces sit in the middle of the grass name

parts.note: Poa is the botanical genus of the meadow grasses
the word in itself, taken as letters
CI is the international code for Côte d'Ivoire, the Ivory Coast
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A tree grows in the Ivory Coast, one standing in a grassy meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but two letters of the wordplay; 'amid' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Poinciana is a genus of tropical flowering trees, including the flamboyant or royal poinciana.

clue.text: Combined contest, half of it in Bath, half London

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the city name Bath
half of a two-letter word is its first letter

parts.note: the word it, taken as written before half is taken

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word keeps the first three letters, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: Sounds like an event staged partly in Bath and partly in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the first letter of 'it' and 'in' puts it into the city name; 'half' keeps the first three letters of the capital. Bath is a city in the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A biathlon is a sporting event combining two disciplines, classically cross-country skiing and rifle shooting.

clue.text: More than one fern hunter hid in a short clump

indicators.note: the hunter is concealed within the other letters, so it goes inside them
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tump is a dialect word for a clump or hillock
the last letter of the clump word
Dian is the poetic form of Diana, the Roman goddess of hunting

explanation.surface: Pictures a hunter crouching hidden in a small clump of vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hid in' sets the huntress inside the rest. The definition is plural because the answer names a genus, a whole group of maidenhair ferns.
explanation.definitionFit: Adiantum is the genus of maidenhair ferns, so the name covers many fern species rather than one.

clue.text: Italian dish, not cold, cooked initially in butter

indicators.note: 'in' puts the pieces inside the word for butter

parts.note: ghi is a variant spelling of ghee, the clarified butter of Indian cooking
no can mean not, as in 'no better'
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: 'initially' takes only the first letter of cooked

explanation.surface: An Italian dish, served hot, is cooked first in butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made from potato or semolina, served as a pasta course.

clue.text: Old-timers' close relationship — I'm in it yet heartlessly messed with

indicators.note: messed with means the letters are disordered and rearranged
heartlessly removes the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the middle letter of yet

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being caught up in something that has been tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' cuts YET to YT, and 'messed with' rearranges IMINIT + YT. 'Old-timers'' marks the answer as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimity is an archaic form of intimacy, a close personal relationship.

clue.text: Article about current exhaust pollution falling

parts.note: the indefinite article
c, for circa, means about
I is the symbol for electric current
to drain someone is to exhaust them

explanation.surface: A newspaper report on how vehicle exhaust pollution is falling.
explanation.walkthrough: Exhaust looks like car fumes and falling like a decrease; exhaust is the verb, and falling describes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made acidic by sulphur and nitrogen emissions, so it is airborne pollution that comes down from the sky.

clue.text: Fabulous bird in pub — brutal!

the huma is a mythical Persian bird that never lands

explanation.surface: Someone admires a stunning woman in a pub, then remarks how harsh it all is.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous looks like 'wonderful' and bird like British slang for a woman; it means a bird of fable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe cruelty without pity or compassion, behaviour lacking the kindness expected of people.

clue.text: Publicise new club at St Andrews

parts.note: to air views is to publicise them
N is the abbreviation for new

clue.text: Performances mostly worthy of credit

clue.text: African seaman cutting beer? There's no fluke with it, perhaps

clue.text: As some characters, about twenty-seven, turned up

the answer to clue 27 down

clue.text: Soundly test child's toy craft ruler

clue.text: Shyly plagiarise work steadily, missing page more than once

clue.text: Singer from Otello hogging front of Met stage for Butterfly?

clue.text: Doomed to get reduced intelligence?

taken as written

clue.text: Not easily getting gear over-the-counter in US city? Heroin's included in that
